about: DRAFT coach wording, NOT APPROVED. Added 23 October 2026 (Stage G of the design of 25 October 2026, section 3) for the goal version of the build-out activity: the words the renderer (back/src/system/rendering/render-concrete-game.ts) may say for an object a game sets out and for a team that scores at an object, keyed by register vocabulary values (the O2.kind of an object, the V1.kind of a scoring event) and never by an activity, a goal or an element, so no scoring kind or sport noun is written in an engine file (the design's no-exception ratchet: 'New wording for a goal comes from data, never from a branch beside ZONE_ENTRY_EVENT'). Every sentence built from these words is DRAFT, awaiting his approval, and is shown to an administrator as draft wording; none is approved-coach-wording.json, which changes only after his approval. The words follow his rulings, each quoted verbatim with the reply it is filed in ('basis'); where a clause states a rule of the game, the game must entail it where it is said (the renderer's gates, named per clause), and fidelity holds every sentence to the game as it holds every other DRAFT sentence. Read through AUDITS_DIR, so the bundled server finds it in dist/knowledge; build.js copies it. Nothing served for real uses it until the goal version is selectable: its two open decisions (goal suitability, the penalty area) are his.

entryShape.objectKinds: [{ kind: a member of the register's O2.kind vocabulary, standsOutsideArea: the words said after an object of this kind is placed on an end line, saying where its structure stands (a clause, starting ', '), basis: { words: [his words verbatim], citedAs } }] - said only for an object the game places on an end line with no depth inside the area (its realized along interval one point on an end line)
entryShape.facings: [{ facing: a member of the register's O6.facing vocabulary (the facing row objectGeometry names), words: the words said, after ', ', for an object placed facing that way (no slot), basis }] - added by the Stage G review fix, 23 October 2026, so the words for a facing come from data as every other word of the placing sentence does; a facing with no entry has no words, so the placing sentence is not said and fidelity refuses the game
entryShape.scoringAtObjects: [{ event: a member of the register's V1.kind vocabulary whose target, by the register's roleScoring.targetTypes map, is an object of targetKind, targetKind: a member of the O2.kind vocabulary, lead: how a team scores by the event, with the slots {carrier} (the kind of the object played with) and {target} (the kind of the object scored at), basis, clauses: [{ text: the words said after the lead, with the slot {carrier} only, starting with their own joining punctuation, states: MEANING (what the event itself counts, said wherever the lead is said) | NO_OTHER_SCORE (that nothing else scores for the team, said only where the team scores by an event of its own, register row B9, and no occurrence that also counts, row V27, names its team), basis }] }]
entryShape.normalLaws: { words: the one Coach Details sentence the d26 design holds for the sport's normal laws (whole, no slot: the sport's noun is data here), held: why it is held and not said, basis } - added 23 October 2026 (H2, the d26 design's build step 2, section 3.2: 'One DRAFT Coach Details sentence, "Otherwise, normal soccer rules apply", with the sport noun from data.' 'The served zone text is unchanged until he approves.'). HELD: no renderer reads it; the default-laws account in the administrator's review evidence shows it as held

normalLaws.held: Held, not served: no activity says it until he approves the sentence, and the served zone version's text stays as it is until then (the d26 design's section 3.2). It is shown to an administrator beside the default-laws account.

words: The normal Laws of the Game should apply by default wherever they are applicable, unless an activity introduces an explicit, knowledge-authorized modification.
The governing principle is to inherit established sport rules and explicitly define only the necessary departures.
